runtime_prompt_en: A naturalistic documentary photograph of military unit duty, on a quiet airbase apron just before sunrise. The reference-guided main subject is performing a military support task: a fictional adult woman in faded olive maintenance coveralls crouches beside the nose wheel of a parked gray military transport aircraft, checking that a heavy yellow wheel chock is seated firmly against the tire before the incoming crew takes responsibility. Her oval face, large dark brown eyes, small straight nose, softly rounded lips, and short dark brown bob with fine separated fringe follow the supplied face-and-hair reference. Her face is visible in three-quarter view, her attention on the check, a small tired softness at the mouth lending warmth to her composed concentration. Both boots rest on the concrete and her knees bend naturally; her right hand presses the top of the yellow wedge, whose sloping face touches the front lower surface of the black tire, while her left hand rests on her own bent knee. A second ground-crew member kneels a little farther to camera right, holding a clipboard against their raised thigh and marking the inspection sheet with a pencil while watching the chock check. The main subject glances up toward that teammate at the instant the pencil records the completed inspection, making the handover feel shared and consequential. The aircraft nose gear, the entire wheel, the wedge-to-tire contact, both connected arms and the two faces remain visible together. A broad aircraft fuselage and high-mounted wing extend behind them, with a hangar door and sparse service carts farther away. Muted steel-blue dawn light meets a warm hangar spill on her cheek and the worn cotton folds. A low, unobtrusive three-quarter camera position, medium-wide horizontal frame, natural 40mm perspective and moderate depth of field connect the two workers with the equipment; documentary skin texture, quiet material wear, a grounded working moment.
